stances_toward.note: No mutual-defence treaty, but a treaty-level de facto alignment against the same Chinese pressure: the Reciprocal Access Agreement entered into force on 11 Sep 2025 (the Philippines' third such pact after the US and Australia), the ACSA was signed on 15 Jan 2026 and in force on 22 Aug 2026, and Official Security Assistance has delivered radars and boats with TC-90 trainers and retired Abukuma-class escorts planned. The grade is ally by structure (binding access and logistics treaties, joint exercises); no source calls the pair 'allied' - hence B and not A.

stances_toward.note: A labour relationship with repeated friction: 267,259 Filipinos live in Kuwait (5% of residents), most of them domestic workers. The Philippines banned deployment in February 2018 after a worker's body was found in a freezer, and lifted it after a May 2018 agreement on migrant workers' rights; Kuwait's foreign minister condemned a 2023 murder, a Kuwaiti court sentenced an employer to death for the 2019 killing of a Filipina worker, and Manila weighed reviewing the labour agreement in 2023. Partner despite recurring bans and protests, because Kuwait needs the workers and Manila needs the remittances. Sources for 2024-26 were not found in this pass (confidence C). Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: Unofficial ties only; the relevant fact is geography. The Bashi Channel and Batanes sit 100 nautical miles from Taiwan, and Marcos has said the Philippines would be 'pulled in' by a war over Taiwan. In Feb 2026 Manila, Washington and Tokyo ran their first Multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity over the Bashi Channel (Taiwan not a participant). Reports of Philippine-Taiwanese coast-guard patrols and Taiwanese observers at Kamandag 2025 rest on a single Washington Post account relayed by Taiwan News and are unconfirmed. Partner, with trend warming, is our reading (confidence C); not an ally, since no document binds Manila to anything. Bond - none: shared interest in the strait, no tie underneath.
